newsitem.title: USA: Ill. Gov signs $18.18 bln gen fund budget for '98.
newsitem.headline: Ill. Gov signs $18.18 bln gen fund budget for '98.

text.p: Illinois Gov. Jim Edgar has approved an $18.18 billion general fund budget for the upcoming fiscal year.
The budget for fiscal 1998 signed by Edgar Wednesday includes a $342 million increase in elementary and secondary education funding.
About $100 million of that increase has been funded through projected state revenue growth, however, and Edgar said in a statement that the budget falls short of his education funding goals.
Illinois lawmakers rejected Edgar's proposal to increase the state income tax 25 percent to provide $600 million to schools and another $900 million in property tax cuts.
"Despite the rhetoric that channeling natural revenue growth to our schools can solve the problem, the reality is that it can't," Edgar said.
The budget signed by Edgar totals $35.618 billion for all funds and includes an authorization for $167 million of bonds for capital projects.
